title: The Smart Kettle
story:
Grandad's new kettle could be switched on with a phone, and he was not sure he liked that. On Sunday his granddaughter Amina helped him set it up. They plugged the kettle into the wall and held a button until a blue light blinked. Amina's phone found the kettle and asked for the home network name.

Grandad read the password from a card in the drawer and typed it slowly. The app said the kettle was connected. Amina chose eighty degrees, because he liked tea that was hot but not boiling. Now the app could stop at the right point. A beep told them the water was ready.

On Monday Grandad was in the garden when his phone, left on a chair, woke the kettle by accident. He had dropped the phone into his pocket without locking the screen, and the app button was easy to touch. The water had steamed for many minutes.

After school Amina changed the settings. She turned off control from the lock screen and added a four-number code. She also set a rule that the kettle could run for only five minutes. Grandad practised the steps twice. He still liked the old switch for a quick cup, but the app was useful when he wanted tea at four o'clock. That afternoon he started it from the garden on purpose, and the beep sounded just as he came inside.
